event.description: Split QKV into explicit query, key, and value maps and tie only the value map across the two blocks; retain independent Q/K maps, shared attention outputs, shared final/pre-attention normalization scale, rank-4 tied tokens, factorized rank-3 positions, d=14, ff=19, and 75000 steps.
event.proposal: Family: parameter tying. Retained incumbent is attempt-0059 with 2676 parameters at 99.360000%, a +0.360000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: the most recent accepted result is attempt-0059, final-to-pre-attention normalization-scale tying (2676, 99.36%); the most recent failed result is attempt-0060, within-block pre-norm scale sharing, an optimization failure plateauing near 94% validation after 75000 steps; 12 prior parameter-tying macro attempts. Hypothesis: the value transform is a reusable content basis across two attention stages, particularly because the downstream attention-output map is already shared, while queries and keys must remain layer-specific to form distinct causal attention patterns. Refactoring the combined QKV linear map into equivalent separate maps is parameterization-preserving; tying only the two 14x14 value maps is the representational compression, not scalar pruning. It removes 196 actual parameters (2676 to 2480). It is more informative than tying Q or K across depth because it preserves attention-score formation and tests only cross-stage value content reuse.
